description: This file defines a PySide6 GUI dialog class for parameter panel in the BORIS behavior analysis software. It manages user interactions for selecting subjects, behaviors, and time intervals related to behavioral observations, and provides methods to extract behaviors based on observations and subjects.

classes.name: Param_panel
classes.description: A dialog class for managing parameter inputs related to behavioral observation analysis, including subject and behavior selection and time interval configuration.

methods.name: __init__(self, parent=None)
methods.description: Initializes the Param_panel dialog, sets up UI components, connects signals to slots, and prepares the widget for user interaction.

methods.name: cb_exclude_non_coded_modifiers_visibility(self)
methods.description: Sets visibility and enabled state of the non-coded modifiers checkbox based on other checkbox state.

methods.name: rb_time_interval_selection(self, button)
methods.description: Configures the time interval widgets and visibility based on selected time mode and current data context.

methods.name: subjects_button_clicked(self, command)
methods.description: Handles bulk selection/deselection/reversal of subject checkboxes.

methods.name: behaviors_button_clicked(self, command)
methods.description: Handles bulk selection/deselection/reversal of behavior items in the list.

methods.name: ok(self)
methods.description: Collects selected subject and behavior data from UI and accepts the dialog.

methods.name: behavior_item_clicked(self, item)
methods.description: Toggles the checked state of behaviors when a category is clicked, applying bulk check/uncheck to items in that category.

methods.name: extract_observed_behaviors(self, selected_observations, selected_subjects)
methods.description: Extracts unique behavior codes from selected observations and subjects within the dataset.

methods.name: cb_changed(self)
methods.description: Updates behavior check states based on current subject selections, reflecting observed behaviors.
